faqs.question: What is Environmental Engineering course?
faqs.answer: Environmental Engineering courses basically focus on improving the overall quality of the world around us and coming up with solutions to environmental problems. Along with the Engineering curriculum, students get to study a lot about Soil Science, Biology, Chemistry as well as Mathematics. Some of the most common topics covered in Environmental Engineering courses include chemical compound disposal, petroleum product manufacturing, mineral mining, and the overall biological understanding of the ecosystem. The sole purpose of environmental engineers is to look after the upkeep of rural and urban settings and ensure that they are in a healthy state. know more about - Environmental Engineering Career

faqs.question: What skills will I learn from the BTech Environmental Engineering course?
faqs.answer: The BTech Environmental Engineering course teaches you a lot of important, transferable skills during the coursework duration. The skills are not necessarily to be learned within the four walls of the classroom but can be learned via internships, lab work, and workshop sessions. Here are a few important skills that you'll learn : Strong Knowledge of Environmental Awareness Understanding of Pollution Control and Wastewater Management Strategies Critical Thinking & Problem-Solving Aptitude Project Management Creative and Analytical Approach Good Industrial Knowledge CAD Proficiency Excellent Communication

faqs.question: Does Environmental Engineering curriculum have Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Hi, Yes, Environmental Engineering graduates require a basic understanding of Mathematics in order to design and operate models and systems which are environment friendly. faqs.question: What do Environmental Engineers do?
faqs.answer: Hi, Environmental engineers invent the ways to protect the environment from harmful waste, bacteria, chemicals etc. Examples of Environmental Engineering work incorporate building dams, municipal water supply, systems for recycling and reusing waste, wastewater treatment facilities, plants to desalinate ocean water for irrigation of crops, refineries that reduce air pollutants, etc. To become an effective environmental engineer, he must possess problem-solving skills, interpersonal skills, reading, writing, knowledge about nature, etc. know more about - Environmental Engineering Career

faqs.question: How can I apply for BTech Environmental Engineering admission: Online or Offline?

blocks.value: You have both options available depending on the particular college you wish to apply to . A majority of the top BTech Environmental Engineering colleges release the application forms in the online mode on their university/college portal, which allows you to fill out the forms from the comfort of your homes without having to travel to the respective college.

Some colleges may still follow the old approach of offline form filling at the college window. So, you should go to the official college websites to check their application methods and then apply accordingly . The basic steps are uploading the scanned copies of the relevant docs and submitting the application fee.

faqs.question: What is the selection criterion for BTech Environmental Engineering admission?

blocks.value: The selection criterion for BTech Environmental Engineering admission is a combination of both Class 12 merit and entrance test scores . Top colleges like the IITs and NITs ask for valid JEE Advanced and JEE Main exam scores respectively, while a few other private colleges consider the Class 12 board exam marks and may take extra rounds like the GD or PI.
You can go to the college websites for BTech Environmental Engineering to have better clarity about their eligibility requirements and admission procedure.

The relaxation in marks is generally 5%, which may vary on the basis of the institution offering the course. For accurate information around the reservation policies for the course, you will have to check the official websites of the colleges you're targeting.

Environmental Engineering Syllabus: List of Subjects
The list of typical core subjects and typical elective subjects have been listed in the tables available below:
Typical core subjects for Environmental Engineering

value: Basic Environmental Engineering and Elementary Biology

The syllabus is a unification of environmental concepts, engineering, and sciences. Students understand the basic principles of environmental particles and develop new solutions, using engineering for the environment, industry, and other fields. It starts with ecology concepts such as the importance of the environment. It then talks about the spiralling rate of population and how human beings now require more land for living. However, this has led to large-scale deforestation, which will destroy the planet. Acid rain, greenhouse effect, smog, environmental pollution, and depletion of the ozone layer are some of the other topics discussed. Some parts of the syllabus are: Environmental pollution Large-scale deforestation Depletion of the ozone layer Acid rain Creation of greenhouse effect Smog
Water Supply and Wastewater Disposal Systems

Wastewater treatment systems comprise storage tanks, reaction vessels, and sludge tanks. These systems also include equipment such as mixers and watering machines, ph adjustment and polymer make-up units, and filter presses. Some parts of the syllabus are: Dimensions and units Water sources Water quantity, process description of conventional water treatment Design of individual unit processes Water treatment plant layout Sewage Concept

The atmospheric particles affect the balance between shortwave and longwave radiation. The climate effects of greenhouse gases can be increased or decreased, depending on if the clouds cause warming (due to an amplified greenhouse effect) or cooling (due to an increased shortwave albedo). Humidity or dust cause an enhancement of IR opacity and, in turn, raise the adequate level of radiative cooling. Some parts of the syllabus are: Industrial processes Dust storms Natural PM Particles from power generators Sea spray

Human activities produce large amounts of solid waste. Inadequate or inappropriate management of these byproducts can have serious public health consequences and harmful effects on the environment. Various categories of solid waste produce different kinds of negative impacts. Much of this subject is devoted to the functional aspects of solid waste management programmes, particularly storage, collection, and disposal of solid waste. Some parts of the syllabus are: Identification and clarification of hazardous waste Storage and collection Transfer and transport Physical and chemical treatment Biological treatment

value: Microbial biotechnology uses non-human or non-plant microbes for purposes such as synthesis, cellulose production, bio-isolation, and knowledge. The field of microbial biotechnology also covers methods of manipulation and control such as gene knockout.

blocks.value: Environmental Engineering Syllabus in Detail

The syllabus for BTech in Environmental Engineering may vary from one university to the other, but the subjects are more or less the same. Here is an overview of the core or elective subjects taught from the first to the eighth semester in the course:

value: Introduction to Environmental Particles and Effects
Introduction to Environmental Particles and Effects

The size of the particles is very important when it comes to health. The smaller they are, the greater their potential to cause breathing issues or enter your blood or lungs. The smallest size can be 10 micrometres. Fine particulates (PM2.5) have been found to be the main cause of haze, or reduced visibility, in some parts of the US. The issue has been even more pronounced in wilderness areas and national parks. In most cases, plants and vegetation can also be affected by acid properties.

The objective of the course is to provide students with the basic knowledge of environmental chemistry and microbiology and allow them to use that for understanding and solving environmental problems. Some of the topics covered in Environmental Chemistry are a review of basic concepts, equilibria, equilibrium constants and activity, kinetics, and acidity versus alkalinity. Primary topics discussed in environmental microbiology are microorganisms, bacteria, fungi, algae, protozoa, and other higher forms. There are several types of viruses as well. These microscopic organisms cause diseases in human beings. Fortunately, they can be controlled with proper measures. Microbes are not just pollutants, but also energy sources.
Hydraulics and water resource engineering are concerned with designing water systems. This includes designing bridges, dams, channels, canals, and levees.
Environmental hydraulics is the scientific study of natural water flows and their related transport and transformation processes in environmental systems.

Hazardous waste can be taken care of by following biological, chemical, physical and thermal methods. Chemical methods include chemical reactions such as ion exchange, precipitation, and oxidation-reduction. Biological methods involve microorganisms such as bacteria or fungi. Physical methods treat the waste by grinding it into a powder or boiling it before releasing it into the environment (in-situ treatment). High-temperature incineration can detoxify particular organic wastes and burn off toxic combustion gases.

As an undergraduate student, one would study Rock Mechanics, Soil-Structure Interactions, Ground Improvement Techniques, Plastic Equilibrium in Soils, Geotechnical Earthquake Engineering, Foundation Dynamics, and Risk and Reliability in Geotechnical Engines.
There are three types of sewage wastewater: industrial sewage, domestic sewage, and stormwater. Domestic sewage is also called a sanitary sewer. Industrial sewage is water used in manufacturing.
There are a variety of technologies that are used for desalination, but the most important of these are reverse osmosis (RO), ion exchange (IX), electrodialysis (ED), and electrolysis.
Students work on real-world projects comprising environmental study, analysis of particles, the study of pollution levels, etc.

blocks.value: Environmental Engineering Syllabus for Distance Programme

Students who can’t afford full-time courses can get their degrees through distance education. Students who don’t meet the eligibility requirements for full-time courses can also opt for a distance/part-time programme. The syllabus of the distance education programme is similar to the regular one. The evaluation format (20% for internal assessment and 80% for the end semester examination) is also similar.
The top colleges for distance education are MIT Manipal, COEP Pune, BIT Mesra, Manav Bharti University, Sikkim Manipal University, Delhi University, and Vinayaka Mission University.
Specialisations offered in Environmental Engineering

Environmental Engineering is an umbrella term used for covering expansive topics such as air particles, geological aspects, engineering, waste management, and many more. The applications of this course spread far and wide to sectors such as agriculture, animal husbandry, pollution control, energy production and conservation, eco-conservation, vaccines, insecticides, development of sewage systems, and fertilisers.

value: Sludge Treatment Physical Water Treatment Chemical Treatment Sewage System Analysis Water Channel Analysis Recycling Anaerobic Digestion

Ion Exchange Precipitation Oxidation-Reduction Toxicity Measurement

Specialisation in Solid and Hazardous Waste Management allows students to learn in detail about plant ion exchange, the definition of waste, and the mechanism of managing solid waste. Upon completion, students get involved in solid and hazardous waste management research.
Designing Bridges Dams Channels  Canal  Levees
The specialisation offers a deep insight into the relationships among various water resources.

Environmental Studies explains several environmental particles and their impact on human and plant lives.

This acclaimed book for classical environmental engineering covers basic theoretical information and the study of trends through experiments and reasoning.

The author breaks the confusing concepts of complex wastewater treatment procedures into easy-to-understand steps in this book.

The authors help students strengthen their ability to calculate waste levels in a water body by providing many problems at the end of every chapter.

career.title: Environmental Engineering Career Guide: Roles, Salary & Future Scope
intro: Environmental Engineering careers in India can lead to a sustainable future and decent earning potential for fresh graduates. For students who are passionate about the environmental world and want to earn a handsome income, they are in for an exciting ride when it comes to pursuing Environmental Engineering courses after Class 12.

Environmental engineers work to improve problems that have to do with waste disposal and recycling, public health, environmental sustainability, and air and water quality, and find ecological solutions for the same. The sole purpose of environmental engineers is to look after the upkeep of rural and urban settings and ensure that they are in a healthy state. They design, construct, and manage different environmental and waste management systems.

Some of the highest paying Environmental Engineering jobs for freshers in India include Environmental Conservation Scientist, Environmental Engineer, Environmental Health and Safety Manager, Hydrologist, Natural Sciences Manager, Environmental Policy Analyst, Chemical Engineer, etc. The average Environmental Engineering salary in India is between INR 5 LPA and INR 7 LPA . The salary offered to environmental enthusiasts depends on various factors like experience, skill set, academic qualification, and company location.

The Environmental Engineering career scope is vast and continuously evolving because of the shift in focus towards public safety and sustainability. Top work sectors for Environmental Engineering graduates in India are government agencies, waste management and recycling, transportation, consulting firms, energy sector, research and development, etc. Prominent Environmental Engineering recruiters in India included companies such as Tetra Tech, Central Pollution Control Board, Enviro Analysts & Engineering Pvt. Ltd., Doshion Ltd., NALCO, AECOM, Paramount Ltd., Brunel India Pvt. Ltd., etc.
